heard: 10 billion light years across, a cosmic wall exists that shouldn't. In November 2013, astronomers Istvan Horvath, John Hakila, and Zolt Bagali analyzed gamma-ray bursts using data from space telescopes. Because these explosions are extremely luminous and track massive star formations, researchers used them to map unseen matter. They mapped the Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall, spanning about 10% of the entire observable universe. This structure shatters the cosmological principle, which states the universe should be uniform on large scales. John Hakila admitted that he would have thought this structure was too big to exist. Some studies argue it could simply be a statistical illusion in incomplete datasets. Until future missions decide the debate, 10 billion light years of galaxies remain an impossible anomaly.
